title: A constitutive theory of active stress that can be inverted for a mechanical task

concept.text: The proposed innovation is a quantitative theory that connects the components and internal energy use of an active material to the forces it produces and its response to deformation. In an actomyosin gel, for example, independently measured motor activity, filament turnover, alignment and interactions would become inputs for predicting stress, stiffness, dissipation and flow. Active-gel theory already describes crosslinked filaments acted on by molecular motors; the target here is a sufficiently predictive and transferable constitutive relationship to support material design.

Proposed capability: use the same framework in both directions. First, predict how a defined active material responds to imposed deformation. Then start from a mechanical task, such as sustaining a specified channel-flow speed against an opposing pressure difference, and determine realizable material properties and activity levels that could deliver it. The inverse calculation would combine the constitutive law with device geometry, boundary conditions, energy supply and stability. Successful transfer would require meeting the task without adjusting the active-stress coefficient specifically to fit the finished device.

significance.text: Active materials convert supplied energy into internal stresses and motion. Existing theory and experiments already establish spontaneous flow and actuation, including sustained internally driven motion in confined channels. Their engineering promise therefore extends beyond selecting how a passive material resists a load: activity can contribute mechanical work. A transferable component-to-stress theory would make that contribution more predictable and controllable. The 2025 motile-active-matter roadmap documents limitations caused by simplifying assumptions and idealized geometries and identifies predictive models grounded in first principles and detailed experimental conditions as valuable for design.

Conditional significance: if forward predictions and inverse designs succeeded across a declared material class, engineers could specify an active fluid or gel by the mechanical function it must perform, rather than relying on repeated device-specific adjustment. A demonstrated example would be a suspension that delivers a stated flow against a stated pressure load; further possibilities include materials designed to yield under selected loading conditions or change their mechanical response as activity changes. These would be substantial advances in rheological design, but a constitutive equation alone would not guarantee feasible fabrication, sufficient power, stable operation or an acceptable operating lifetime.

The equilibrium analogy has limits. Internal energy consumption means that a passive equilibrium free-energy description alone cannot account for the full active mechanical response; this does not imply that passive elastic contributions or equilibrium concepts have no useful role in a larger model. Likewise, a successful synthetic-material design law would not by itself establish control over development, fibrosis or metastasis. Those applications would require additional discoveries linking cell regulation, remodeling and biological outcomes to the mechanical variables the theory predicts.

missing_breakthrough.text: The targeted breakthrough is a transferable quantitative link between independently measured microscopic activity and macroscopic stress under imposed flow. The documented challenge is limited predictive capability in existing models and the need to include realistic experimental conditions. The supplied evidence does not establish that every active-gel coefficient lacks molecular determination, that external deformation is universally the weakest part of existing theories, or that the complete proposed capability remained unavailable on 1 November 2026.

Engineering synthesis: a useful law would need to connect motor-generated forces, filament organization, turnover and relaxation while the material is being deformed. Activity, structure and stress can influence one another, so parameters measured in one preparation or flow may not transfer automatically to another. The concrete challenge is to identify which component and interaction measurements suffice, which evolving internal variables must be tracked, and where a continuum description remains reliable. A statistical-mechanical derivation could provide this connection, but the essential outcome is validated prediction and design rather than a particular derivation method.

Nonlinear rheology supplies demanding tests of such a theory. June 2026 simulations of a coarse-grained Voronoi cell model report yielding, shear thinning, continuous and discontinuous shear thickening, and shear jamming. These results motivate testing multiple flow regimes and transitions, but they isolate shape-driven physics using thermal fluctuations rather than explicit motor-driven activity. They therefore do not establish experimental shear thickening in living monolayers or resolve how motor and filament parameters determine those regimes.

Device design adds another barrier: a local stress prediction must produce a consistent flow solution in a particular geometry. The framework must account for boundaries, confinement, energy delivery and the stability of the desired motion. The roadmap's discussion of active-flow control and predictive multiphysics modeling supports this broader challenge. Demonstrating internally driven channel motion is a foundation for a pumping task, but does not by itself establish a specified speed against a specified opposing pressure.

current_state.text: Active-gel physics was an established framework by the 3 February 2015 review by J. Prost, F. Jülicher and J.-F. Joanny. The material retained in the supplied review includes an abstract describing crosslinked filaments acted on by molecular motors and figure captions connecting the discussion to cytokinesis and cortical flows in the Caenorhabditis elegans embryo. Access was limited to a subscription preview, so this evidence supports the framework and those biological connections without establishing the full theoretical treatment or the earlier claim about its explanation of defect motion.

The 2025 motile-active-matter roadmap, identified in the supplied research as published on 7 April 2025, documents existing actuation and spontaneous unidirectional fluid motion in confined periodic channels. It also identifies predictive limitations associated with simplified models and idealized geometries, and calls for models that incorporate first principles and detailed experimental conditions. Its discussion includes challenges in active-flow control and in integrating actuation, sensing and computation into engineered function. The retained extraction is partial and truncates within section 10; it supports these specific dated findings rather than a comprehensive account of every active-material capability.

The June 2026 preprint “Universal scaling in the rheology of dense cellular systems,” dated 13 June in the supplied research, reports constant-stress simulations of a two-dimensional, coarse-grained Voronoi cell model. Reported regimes include yielding, shear thinning, continuous and discontinuous shear thickening, and shear jamming, together with scaling collapses. The model uses thermal fluctuations to isolate shape-driven rheology, rather than explicitly representing motor-driven activity. Its fitted scaling framework predicts flow boundaries within the model, so it contains predictive rheological content; it does not demonstrate molecular-to-device inverse design or experimental living-tissue thickening. The supplied review retained the paper and supplement, but did not independently inspect the graphical data. No later peer-reviewed publication status is established by these inputs.

The research cites the 24 April 2024 review “Active viscoelastic models for cell and tissue mechanics” and attributes to it a limitation concerning response to external deformation. No source text was retained for that citation in the supplied review, so that characterization cannot be confirmed here. This access limitation leaves the assertion unresolved; it does not establish that the assertion or review is incorrect.

The research also records a February 2025 article titled “Progress in rheology of active colloidal systems” in the Current Opinion rheology collection. Its full text was not opened in the research pass, and no collection artifact was retained for the supplied review. The title and date consequently remain unverified within this evidence set, and the entry supplies no substantive evidence about the article's findings.

Evidence-scope synthesis: these dated findings establish foundations and relevant predictive-design challenges, but do not establish either achievement or continued absence of the full proposed capability as of 1 November 2026. The supplied freshness record is empty, and retrieval dates alone do not demonstrate a bounded search for subsequent progress.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed forward demonstration: select a defined actomyosin gel or cell-monolayer system, identify the applicable material class, and independently measure the component, interaction and turnover parameters required by the theory. Before comparing with the target rheology, specify predictions for storage and loss moduli, which measure elastic storage and viscous dissipation, and for the steady flow curve relating stress to shear rate. Include applicable yielding or shear-jamming boundaries. Declare the frequency range, shear protocol, preparation history, observation time and acceptable prediction errors in advance.
completion_criteria.label: Independently measured parameters predict moduli and steady flow curves

completion_criteria.text: Proposed transition tests should distinguish a yield stress or rate-dependent onset from a yield strain measured under a particular loading history. A single universal strain threshold should not be assumed for yielding or shear jamming. Where the theory predicts several flow regimes, test both the response within each regime and the location and reproducibility of transitions. The Voronoi simulations provide a relevant example of stress-controlled regimes and predictive scaling, but do not establish consensus experimental criteria for active gels.
completion_criteria.label: Flow regimes and transitions match predictions with yielding criteria distinguished

completion_criteria.text: Proposed inverse demonstration: within the framework's validated material class, specify a channel geometry, target flow speed and opposing pressure difference, then use the theory to select a realizable active suspension and operating conditions. Include boundary conditions, energy supply and a stability assessment. Build the device and meet the declared performance and duration tolerances without refitting its active-stress coefficient to the device measurements. If the forward tests use an actomyosin gel while the device uses a materially different suspension, validate that transfer explicitly rather than assuming that a shared description as active matter guarantees it.
completion_criteria.label: Theory-designed device meets flow targets without active-stress coefficient refitting

completion_criteria.text: Proposed reproducibility and practical boundaries: repeat the predictions and device task across independently prepared samples and, preferably, an independent laboratory. Use additional conditions or geometries withheld from model fitting to test transfer. Report failures, parameter uncertainty, energy consumption, operating lifetime and the range over which stable performance is demonstrated. These are proposed convincing demonstrations, not established standards. Finite tests would establish a measured breadth of validity within stated conditions, not literal universality across active materials.
completion_criteria.label: Predictions and device tasks reproduce with practical validity limits reported

related_concepts.text: Roster-based synthesis: RHE-01, “A constitutive closure that still works in a flow it was not fitted to,” shares the requirement of prediction beyond calibration conditions. RHE-05 adds internally powered stress and inverse design for a mechanical task. RHE-04, “Inverse molecular design of nonlinear polymer-melt rheology,” shares the component-to-response and inverse-design ambition, but concerns polymer melts rather than the coupling of internal activity, turnover and mechanics. These overlaps identify common validation challenges without making the concepts interchangeable.

Roster-based synthesis: RHE-02, concerning amorphous yielding and brittle or ductile failure, overlaps with predicting yield boundaries, while RHE-03, concerning dense particulate flow from creep to inertia in arbitrary shapes, overlaps with transferable nonlinear flow laws. Yielding, thickening and jamming in the Voronoi model provide a connection to these neighboring topics. RHE-05 retains its distinct target: predicting and designing stresses generated by energy-consuming activity.

Roster-based synthesis: RHE-06 concerns addressable solid–fluid switching that persists without a sustaining field or particle settling. Switching mechanical states could be relevant to an active-material task, but that persistence requirement differs from predicting continuously powered active stress. RHE-07 concerns measuring local three-dimensional stress without assuming a constitutive law; such measurements could independently test RHE-05 predictions, while remaining a separate measurement capability. The research's reference to an unspecified historical item 6 cannot be identified with RHE-06 merely because both use the number six.

Roster-based synthesis: RHE-08 concerns elasto-inertial turbulence and the drag-reduction ceiling, while RHE-09 concerns computing viscoelastic flow at processing-relevant elasticity. Their overlap with RHE-05 lies in solving complex flow and stability problems once material behavior is specified; their stated targets differ from deriving an active-stress design law. RHE-10 targets magma containing crystals and bubbles, and RHE-11 targets topology-dependent ring-polymer rheology. They share the broader goal of connecting material structure to flow, but address distinct material physics.

Conceptual synthesis: a statistical-mechanical derivation is a possible route to RHE-05 rather than a separate innovation in the supplied roster. Existing active-gel hydrodynamics, spontaneous-flow demonstrations and model tissue scaling are foundations or partial capabilities. None is equivalent, on the supplied evidence, to the complete proposed combination of independently parameterized rheology prediction and validated mechanical-task inversion.

change_log.reason: The review supports a coherent innovation concept even though some supporting assertions and its present-day availability remain unresolved.

change_log.change: Replaced categorical claims that active-gel coefficients are never molecularly determined and that imposed deformation is universally their weakest point with the documented predictive-modeling challenge.
change_log.reason: The retained roadmap supports limitations and design needs, but not those universal assertions.

change_log.change: Recast the June 2026 result as a preprint reporting thermally fluctuating Voronoi-model simulations, and preserved its nonlinear regimes and scaling predictions.
change_log.reason: The work does not demonstrate experimental living-monolayer thickening or explicit motor-driven active-stress design, but its fitted scaling does contain predictive content.

change_log.change: Qualified the free-energy statement and narrowed the claimed explanatory scope of the 2015 review.
change_log.reason: Active response exceeds a passive equilibrium description without rendering all equilibrium contributions unusable; subscription-preview access does not substantiate the earlier defect-motion claim.

change_log.change: Integrated geometry, boundaries, energy supply, stability and material-class transfer into the inverse-design objective.
change_log.reason: A constitutive law must be combined with device physics and realizable material choices to establish the proposed mechanical performance.

change_log.change: Expanded the proposed demonstrations with declared protocols, tolerances, independent preparation, transfer tests and operating boundaries.
change_log.reason: These details make success assessable while avoiding a universal yield-strain assumption or claims of universality from finite tests.

change_log.reason: Neither had retained source text in the supplied review; missing evidence warrants qualification rather than treating the claims as disproven.

change_log.reason: The empty freshness record cannot establish either continued absence or achievement of the complete capability.

unresolved_issues: Whether the full component-to-rheology and mechanical-task inverse-design capability had been achieved by 1 November 2026 remains unresolved because no bounded freshness search is supplied.
The 2024 review's specific characterization of response to external deformation cannot be confirmed without retained source text.
The identity, February 2025 date and substantive findings of the named Current Opinion review remain unverified within the supplied evidence.
The June 2026 preprint's later publication status, independent experimental validation and graphical data assessment are not established by the supplied review.
The material class, required independent measurements, numerical prediction tolerances, pressure load and operating duration for a convincing demonstration remain to be specified.

The asserted overlap with historical item 6 cannot be resolved because that item's wording is absent; it has therefore been retained as an unresolved comparison rather than adopted as an identity claim.

brief.title: Designing materials for the work they need to do
possible: Engineers could start with a job, such as keeping fluid moving against an opposing pressure, and calculate which material and energy supply could deliver it. The same theory would predict how that material bends, resists deformation and flows from measurements of its ingredients.
why: Active materials use supplied energy to generate forces and motion internally. A reliable design theory would let engineers choose that mechanical work in advance, reducing repeated adjustments for each device. It could also help them design materials that change their resistance to deformation as their energy use changes.

sources.who: J. Prost, F. Jülicher and J.-F. Joanny
sources.showed: Their review describes a theory of linked filaments driven by molecular motors, proteins that turn chemical energy into motion.
sources.cited_for: It establishes the theoretical foundation for describing materials that generate internal forces.
sources.not_established: It does not demonstrate a transferable recipe for designing a material to perform a specified mechanical task.

sources.who: Authors of the cell and tissue mechanics review
sources.showed: This is a review of models describing how energy-consuming cells and tissues combine elastic resistance with fluid-like flow.
sources.cited_for: It concerns models of cell and tissue responses to mechanical forces.
sources.not_established: A review of mechanical models does not itself establish successful material design for a specified task.

sources.who: Helen S. Ansell and Daniel M. Sussman
sources.showed: Their preprint reports simulations in which model cell sheets flow more easily, resist flow more strongly or stop flowing under applied forces. A shared mathematical description connects these responses.
sources.quote:
We demonstrate that a universal scaling form collapses
the macroscopic viscosity in these seemingly disparate
regimes, highlighting that the same underlying physical
parameters control the observed nonlinear rheology.
sources.cited_for: The simulations provide demanding examples of changes in flow behavior that a predictive theory should explain.
sources.not_established: The model isolates cell-shape effects without explicit molecular motors; it does not demonstrate living-tissue behavior or device design.

sources.showed: Their roadmap reviews internally driven motion, including flow in confined channels, and identifies limits in models that simplify material behavior and device geometry.
sources.quote: Inspired by biological active systems, various types of autonomous synthetic nano- and micromachines have been designed, which provide the basis for multifunctional, highly responsive, intelligent active materials.
sources.cited_for: Existing motion provides a foundation, while predictive models must account for realistic experimental conditions.
sources.not_established: Internally driven channel flow does not establish a designed speed against a specified opposing pressure.

shown: Researchers have demonstrated sustained, internally driven flow in confined channels, as reviewed by Gompper and collaborators. Ansell and Sussman have also predicted changes in flow behavior within a simulated cell-sheet model. These are foundations for connecting material ingredients to a working device.
missing: A transferable theory must predict forces and flow from independently measured ingredients and energy use while the material is being deformed.
A device designed with that theory must meet a flow target against opposing pressure without adjusting its internal-force parameter afterward.
Repeated tests must establish how well predictions transfer across samples and conditions, alongside power needs, stability and operating lifetime.

milestones.label: Independent measurements predict resistance and flow
milestones.explanation: Ingredient measurements would have to predict elastic response, energy loss and steady flow within declared errors and conditions. This would test whether the theory predicts behavior before it is measured.

milestones.label: Changes between flow states match predictions
milestones.explanation: Tests would have to reproduce predicted flow states and transitions, distinguishing force thresholds from deformation thresholds. This would establish when a material starts flowing or becomes jammed.

milestones.label: A designed device meets its flow target
milestones.explanation: A theory-selected material would have to sustain target flow against opposing pressure without retuning its internal-force parameter. Accounting for boundaries, energy supply and stability would test design in a working device.

milestones.label: Results repeat and practical limits become clear
milestones.explanation: Predictions and device performance would have to repeat across independent samples and conditions excluded from fitting. Measured failures, uncertainty, power use and lifetime would establish the usable range.

uncertain: Which ingredient measurements and changing internal structures are sufficient to predict the material's behavior?
How broadly can a theory transfer between materials and geometries?
What prediction errors, pressure load and operating duration would make a demonstration convincing?

page.title: Constitutive inverse design of active gels
page.definition: A constitutive law—a relation between stress and deformation—predicts the mechanics of motor-driven filament networks from independently measured constituents and energy supply. Inverting the same law selects a realizable composition and operating conditions for a specified mechanical task.

goal.need: Myosin activity increased the stiffness of reconstituted actin networks nearly 100-fold in work published on 19 January 2007. Motor-driven microtubule networks also generate macroscopic fluid transport. A constitutive design law must connect constituent properties with these mechanical responses and device operation; the roadmap identifies predictive models incorporating experimental conditions as necessary for design.

statements.body: The 2025 motile active matter roadmap contributors, section 3 by David Saintillan
statements.quote: Accurate predictive multiphysics models (both analytical and computational) that are based on first principles and account for detailed experimental conditions
statements.context: The passage identifies models needed to support design strategies for active particles and suspensions.

statements.quote: and predict the properties of new materials before creating them in the laboratory.
statements.context: The Animate materials report describes using simulations and machine learning trained on material databases. This is a broader material-design objective.

statements.body: European Commission, Horizon Europe IDAM project
statements.quote: to target and stabilize such spontaneous, collective phase transitions via the development of a novel ID framework.
statements.context: ID means inverse design. The funded objective concerns collective states in active-matter models; it does not specify a constitutive mechanical-task benchmark.

completion.title: An active gel selected by a constitutive law meets a specified mechanical task.
completion.criterion: Within one declared material class, invert a constitutive law to select a new composition and energy supply for a mechanical task, then realize it experimentally without fitting constitutive coefficients to the finished device. For pumping, deliver the specified volumetric flow Q against an opposing pressure difference Δp > 0 for the specified duration. Targets and acceptance tolerances precede fabrication. The same law must already predict imposed-deformation measurements from independently measured inputs. Numerical tolerances, load and duration remain task-specific.
completion.set_by: Atlas fallback; no external completion criterion was found.
completion.basis: Searches covered the motile-active-matter roadmap, the Royal Society's Animate materials report, Horizon Europe IDAM objectives, and rheology standards, benchmarks and prizes. No external test combining constituent-based stress prediction with experimental inverse design of a loaded device was found. This fallback tests that combination within one material class.

milestones.title: Energy supply changes an active gel's measured mechanical response.
milestones.criterion: Under controlled mechanical forcing, an active gel exhibits a change in its stress–deformation response when motor activity changes, resolved beyond measurement uncertainty. This foundation is demonstrated for actomyosin networks: Mizuno et al., published on 19 January 2007, measured ATP-dependent viscoelasticity and nearly 100-fold stiffening. Their opened abstract does not give the independent sample count.
milestones.set_by: Atlas fallback; no external first-demonstration milestone criterion was found.

milestones.title: A microscopic model predicts active-gel stress from filament and motor properties.
milestones.criterion: Predict how macroscopic active stress depends on filament density and motor force–velocity properties in a model resolving individual constituents. The preprint submitted on 5 January 2026 supports this stage for two-dimensional actomyosin simulations. Its baseline contraction averages 72 simulations containing 5,000 filaments each; its motor-stress comparison fits an effective drag of 100 pN·s·µm−1. This result is not peer reviewed and retains a fitted coefficient.
milestones.set_by: Atlas fallback; the cited numerical study supplies evidence, not a field-wide milestone threshold.

milestones.title: Independent constituent measurements predict an active gel's response to imposed deformation.
milestones.criterion: Use independently measured constituent properties and energy supply to predict stress under imposed deformation without fitting to those response data. The 2024 review documents empirical constitutive models and difficulty connecting their parameters to biological processes. The paper accepted on 13 November 2026 infers continuum-model parameters from flow spectra; it does not demonstrate this forward experimental test. Neither source establishes this milestone for either listed material class.
milestones.set_by: Atlas fallback; no external acceptance test for independent-input experimental prediction was found.

milestones.title: The validated law predicts a loaded active-gel device without refitting its material coefficients.
milestones.criterion: With the material coefficients validated in m3 unchanged, predict a device's flow under a specified opposing pressure and energy supply, then verify the prediction experimentally. Composition is supplied rather than selected by inverse design. Published on 12 November 2025, Active nematic pumps reports experimental transport using 1,579 tracer trajectories and pressure buildup in simulations for microtubule–kinesin networks. These results do not establish this coefficient-transfer test.
milestones.set_by: Atlas fallback; no external criterion for transfer from constituent measurements to a loaded device was found.

not_found: No common numerical prediction tolerance, opposing load, operating duration or independent-sample requirement was found for the complete capability.
No experimental demonstration of the complete constituent-to-loaded-device inverse-design chain was found.
The publisher pages for the supplied 2015 active-gel review and Current Opinion rheology sources could not be opened.
